## Problem

Let $H$ be any group. Show that there is a group $G$ containing $H$ as a normal subgroup with the following property:

For every automorphism $\sigma\in \operatorname{Aut}(H)$, there exists an element $g\in G$ such that conjugation by $g$, restricted to $H$, is the given automorphism $\sigma$. In other words, every automorphism of $H$ is obtained as an inner automorphism of $G$ restricted to $H$.

## Remark

When we consider $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(H)$, there may be no element $h_{0}\in H$ such that

$$
\sigma(h)=h_{0}hh_{0}^{-1}
\qquad
\text{for all }h\in H.
$$

That is, not every automorphism of $H$ has to be inner inside $H$.

This problem says that even if $\sigma$ is not inner in $H$, we can enlarge $H$ to a larger group $G$ such that $H\trianglelefteq G$, and then $\sigma$ becomes conjugation by some element of $G$.

## Definition

Recall that if $\varphi:K\to \operatorname{Aut}(H)$ is a homomorphism, then the semidirect product

$$
H\rtimes_{\varphi}K
$$

has underlying set $H\times K$, with multiplication

$$
(h_{1},k_{1})(h_{2},k_{2})
=
\left(h_{1}\varphi(k_{1})(h_{2}),\,k_{1}k_{2}\right).
$$

In this problem, we take

$$
K=\operatorname{Aut}(H)
$$

and define

$$
\varphi:\operatorname{Aut}(H)\to \operatorname{Aut}(H)
$$

by

$$
\varphi(\sigma)=\sigma.
$$

Thus $\varphi$ is the identity map on $\operatorname{Aut}(H)$.

## Solution

Let

$$
G=H\rtimes_{\varphi}\operatorname{Aut}(H),
$$

where

$$
\varphi(\sigma)=\sigma
\qquad
\text{for every }\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(H).
$$

Define

$$
\iota:H\to G
$$

by

$$
\iota(h)=(h,\operatorname{id}_{H}).
$$

We identify $H$ with its image

$$
\iota(H)=H\times\{\operatorname{id}_{H}\}.
$$

First, $\iota$ is an injective homomorphism. Indeed, for $h_{1},h_{2}\in H$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\iota(h_{1})\iota(h_{2})
&=
(h_{1},\operatorname{id}_{H})(h_{2},\operatorname{id}_{H})\\
&=
(h_{1}\operatorname{id}_{H}(h_{2}),\operatorname{id}_{H})\\
&=
(h_{1}h_{2},\operatorname{id}_{H})\\
&=
\iota(h_{1}h_{2}).
\end{aligned}
$$

Also, if $\iota(h)=(1_{H},\operatorname{id}_{H})$, then $h=1_{H}$. Hence $\iota$ is injective.

Therefore,

$$
H\times\{\operatorname{id}_{H}\}\le G.
$$

We now prove that $H\times\{\operatorname{id}_{H}\}$ is normal in $G$.

Take arbitrary

$$
(a,\sigma)\in G
$$

and

$$
(h,\operatorname{id}_{H})\in H\times\{\operatorname{id}_{H}\}.
$$

Since

$$
(a,\sigma)^{-1}
=
\left(\sigma^{-1}(a^{-1}),\sigma^{-1}\right),
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}
(a,\sigma)(h,\operatorname{id}_{H})(a,\sigma)^{-1}
&=
(a,\sigma)(h,\operatorname{id}_{H})
\left(\sigma^{-1}(a^{-1}),\sigma^{-1}\right)\\
&=
(a\sigma(h),\sigma)
\left(\sigma^{-1}(a^{-1}),\sigma^{-1}\right)\\
&=
\left(a\sigma(h)\sigma\bigl(\sigma^{-1}(a^{-1})\bigr),\operatorname{id}_{H}\right)\\
&=
(a\sigma(h)a^{-1},\operatorname{id}_{H}).
\end{aligned}
$$

This belongs to $H\times\{\operatorname{id}_{H}\}$. Hence

$$
H\times\{\operatorname{id}_{H}\}\trianglelefteq G.
$$

Now let $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(H)$. We need to find an element $g\in G$ such that conjugation by $g$, restricted to $H$, gives $\sigma$.

Take

$$
g=(1_{H},\sigma)\in G.
$$

Then

$$
g^{-1}=(1_{H},\sigma^{-1}).
$$

For $h\in H$, consider the corresponding element

$$
(h,\operatorname{id}_{H})\in H\times\{\operatorname{id}_{H}\}.
$$

Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
g(h,\operatorname{id}_{H})g^{-1}
&=
(1_{H},\sigma)(h,\operatorname{id}_{H})(1_{H},\sigma^{-1})\\
&=
(\sigma(h),\sigma)(1_{H},\sigma^{-1})\\
&=
(\sigma(h)\sigma(1_{H}),\operatorname{id}_{H})\\
&=
(\sigma(h),\operatorname{id}_{H}).
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, under the identification

$$
H\cong H\times\{\operatorname{id}_{H}\},
\qquad
h\leftrightarrow (h,\operatorname{id}_{H}),
$$

conjugation by $g=(1_{H},\sigma)$ sends $h$ to $\sigma(h)$. That is,

$$
g(h,\operatorname{id}_{H})g^{-1}
=
(\sigma(h),\operatorname{id}_{H}).
$$

Equivalently,

$$
ghg^{-1}=\sigma(h)
$$

after identifying $H$ with $H\times\{\operatorname{id}_{H}\}$.

Thus every automorphism of $H$ is obtained as conjugation by some element of the larger group

$$
G=H\rtimes \operatorname{Aut}(H).
$$

Hence there exists a group $G$ containing $H$ as a normal subgroup such that every automorphism of $H$ is realized as an inner automorphism of $G$ restricted to $H$.
